releases.title: The Living Archipelago
releases.summary: BR-1.0.0 beta candidate: a physical hangar computer hub, signed pilot contracts, walking ATC, live flight instruments and minigames across the living archipelago. Launch: November 21, 2026 at 4:30 PM CST.
notes: November 14 world refinement: grounded street/garden details across the islands, denser MC planting and correctly spaced crops, real station entrances and fitted plinths, ticket and platform details, full-width rail formation clearance, a rebuilt ribbon document workspace, supported crash/reset handovers and exact cached pedestrian terrain/aircraft queries. Current native frame timings and the outstanding wide-view 50 FPS target are recorded in the county verification report.

November 13 live-flow revision: restored visible island construction, settled crash performance, continuous rendered traffic, shared pedestrian passing, an open MC rail cutting, Free World and rebindable train seating. The accompanying native workflow, storm/photo and ten-minute transport evidence is in artifacts/live_flow_nov13.

November 13 county revision: 38 native hub checks, 14 real monitor-input checks, 26 targeted units and a complete ten-minute transport pass. Seven focused native views average 50.04–70.68 FPS at full resolution with shaders and active simulation. Main loading measured 65.8s.

Rebuilt both station campuses, a four-storey MC garage, actual bus/train/parking journeys, connected farm paths and more livestock/barns, active urban and housing construction, jointed industrial paving and a larger moving population. Lane width, bank, terrain grading and junction reservations follow actual surveyed geometry.

Fixed dogfight return loading/HUD occlusion, mouse cable geometry, ATC look/cursor ownership, intermittent ignition, prop/cloud composition, weather handover, forward logout, single push/pull throttle, pedal targets, crouch view, hangar roof/rain and safe disembark. Writer now has real shaped rich-text editing, formatting, saving and signing. New licensed equipment/vegetation models and industrial typography are credited.

Earlier November 12 source evidence: 98 native workflow/systems checks, 29 safety checks, 20 desktop checks and 15 continuous-path checks pass. 7 focused full-resolution native views average 59.95–60.34 FPS with shaders and active simulation.
Enter Mason County replaces the main Enter button; Pilot Logbook moves into the computer while all existing progression and records are retained. The temporary Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P shortcut is removed.

One continuous camera path flies from the actual menu view into Hangar 01, up the actual stairs and to a randomly selected physical computer; longer fades transfer to the seated NPC. Desktop logout follows the saved path in reverse and fades the orange menu back in.

Five physical workstations have CRT housings, 97 separately shaped and labelled keyboard keys, a wired moving mouse and a fitted right hand. The monitor cursor stays inside the computer; the rebindable look key permits looking away for power controls.

Hold the rebindable computer-power key K for three seconds. The computer starts off; select or confirm an app before powering off and standing up. Every new walking, seat, power and look action is rebindable.
Cloudline Desk 95 adds distinct desktop app logos with names underneath, icon-only taskbar buttons, the Cloudline Start logo, live date/time, searchable app results with Open actions and logout.

Flight Deck offers one real career contract with the actual remaining Shuffle allowance. Cloudline Writer has an editable document, font family/size, bold, italic, underline, clipboard, undo/redo, insert/date/bullets, reading/editing views and session draft saving. Scroll to the signature and sign to activate the actual transport mission.

Air Traffic Control offers 10/15/30-minute duty periods, a live world journey map and four world markers following the open apron around the terminal. Walk into the tower and use Y on a console chair to fade into the existing ATC view; leave the chair to return to walking.

Minigames library, online/offline choices and matchmaking stay inside the physical monitor. Starting a match uses the existing game; Return to Menu automatically seats the character at the same live workstation. Pilot Logbook uses the preserved career/fleet/service record renderer.
Mode assignments change at Hangar 01 computers. Desktop logout returns to the orange main menu; an early ATC departure returns to the physical player rather than teleporting to a mode picker.

Aircraft contacts now confirm registry ownership, current visible source mesh and pose. Self/effect/stale contacts are ignored, occupied cabin surfaces remain pinned, and repositioning clears contact sweeps. A slow taxi bump stops the aircraft rather than causing immediate flight over.
All cabin seats accept a half-second Y hold. Copilot and passenger chairs have no flight authority; only the captain can start or fly. The copilot yoke is lowered and shortened to clear the panel.

Propellers combine actual spinning blades with a filtered dark blade exposure and blur disc in first person. Aborted starting and engine shutdown coast down according to actual shaft RPM, including a longer stop from full power.

Cockpit controls use smaller target radii. Aim at the physical throttle for E/Q; one push/pull callout presents both configured throttle bindings. Hands are fitted nearer the yoke, and aircraft camera motion adds a subtle speed-dependent vibration.

Inverted controls defaults on: the bound pitch-up action points the nose down, and the bound pitch-down action raises it. Turning inversion off restores their usual direction; rebinding still works across civil and fighter flight.

Battery consumption uses real elapsed time so reading dispatch cannot flatten the parked aircraft on the accelerated career clock. Actual out-of-limit instruments pulse with red dial outlines and audible alerts in every camera. Persistent oil/temperature/RPM abuse reduces engine power; prolonged overspeed damages structure. Startup grace and debounce avoid false pressure alarms during normal cranking.
Indoor performance uses exact opaque-wall occluders and bounded monitor-map updates while retaining native image resolution, geometry, materials and shadows.

Two requested rollback checkpoints are retained outside the project: before all changes and after aircraft repairs before the hub. Current source ZIP/cache and all-release comparison are refreshed; all authentic Alpha archives remain unchanged. No compiled app or EXE is packaged. Public launch/countdown remain November 21, 2026, 4:30 PM CST.

Earlier November 12 source (dated evidence): November 12 cockpit update: 58 systems/workflow checks and 74 fitted-cabin checks pass; three current native cockpit views average 60.00–60.00 FPS with full resolution, shaders and live simulation.
Changed captain-seat entry/exit to Y: hold half a second to sit and press to stand. Q decreases throttle correctly while seated in the cockpit; E increases throttle after starting.
Hold C for smooth 2.6x optical zoom toward the current gaze; release C smoothly restores normal view. V cycles flight cameras; the previous default C-camera binding migrates to V.

Rebuilt the attached analogue flight deck with six flight dials, eleven engine/electrical dials, a three-hand altimeter and Kollsman window, precision ticks, operating arcs, moving cards/needles and live warning lamps.

All physical flight readings use actual simulation state: IAS, MSL altitude, pitch/bank, gyro heading, filtered VSI, electric turn rate and an independent slip ball. Corrected heading direction and the conventional VSI zero/climb/descent dial.

Oil quantity is an eight-quart-capacity consumed store. Pump pressure responds to RPM, temperature and supply; starvation affects lubrication health/power. CHT and EGT follow load/cooling rather than decorative RPM labels.

Electrical gauges show stored battery charge/current and alternator bus voltage, including master-off and engine-off discharge. Engine-driven vacuum spins up/down the attitude and heading gyros; low-pressure/fuel/voltage/vacuum lamps use those states.

Physical readings update at 29.42 Hz in the focused native run; static engraved artwork is cached at double panel resolution. The external engine HUD shares the same pressure, quantity, temperature, voltage, current and vacuum state.

Verified repeated Y seating, Q throttle-down, V camera selection, C zoom/release, pause recovery and ignition shutdown through the actual keyboard path. Captured the physical panel in the live ground and airborne cockpit.

Refreshed the verified current BR-1.0.0 source snapshot, installed launcher source and all-release comparison; historical Alpha archives remain intact. Public launch remains Saturday November 21, 2026 at 4:30 PM CST.

November 11 county revision (dated prior evidence): Final restored-resolution source verification: fifteen focused, unpaused Apple M4/Metal views average 55.41–97.15 FPS with native 3D scale 1 and shaders on, including 0% and default 80% pixelation. All pass the 50 average-FPS gate; the 58+ soft target is not met in every heavy view and individual slower frames remain recorded. Repeated real-key boarding, seating, engine, reset and storm/menu transitions pass 101 checks; ratio/geometry tests pass 1,614 and all three civil cabin profiles pass 74. City courtyard parking has 144 correctly owned cars, zero misplaced cars and about 0.04 m footing offset. No compiled app or EXE is packaged.

Rebuilt MC with five connected neighbourhoods, a terminal borough, 420 street-facing buildings, local services, street furniture and additional road traffic; protected runways, taxiways, rail corridors and approach clearances.

Rebuilt NMC as connected commercial, residential, industrial and agricultural districts: 1,147 frontage buildings, through streets inside the housing area, real workshops/warehouses, three working container courts and ten connected crop fields with a grouped farm service yard.

Individually revised all twelve satellite settlements with interior streets, dedicated market/workshop/rescue/quarry/research/visitor sites and distinct woodland layouts. The complete county contains 2,711 nonoverlapping frontage parcels across fourteen islands.

Corrected the metre/layout conversions for lot footprints, setbacks, roads, terminal heights, windsocks, boats, lookout equipment and trees. The human remains approximately 1.75 m and the three moored cargo hulls remain 192 m.

Replaced oversized parking markings with 544 shared MC bays measuring 2.75 by 5.5 m, properly fitted parked cars and usable aisles. Rebuilt the NMC park-and-ride with fifty full-size bays and a clear pedestrian approach.
Fixed city courtyard parking ownership: NMC-local parked cars now belong to NMC, removing static car formations above MC and populating the intended city parking courts.

Restored full-size train bodies: eighteen-metre passenger coaches and twelve-to-fourteen-metre freight/front vehicles. The 113.25 m, 86.20 m and 121.74 m consists fit the 180/168 m platforms and retain bounded screw couplings, buffers, gangways and interiors through curves.

Rebuilt the road tunnel around a consistent carriageway, filled shoulders and founded portal faces; matched road-bridge deck, guards, beams and support widths. Removed the giant arch around a narrow road.

Matched the hangar lead-in centreline and 0.15 m paint width to the interior stripe, repaired the perimeter taxi pavement width, and retained runway stencils/lines to a reasonable flight-view distance without simplifying their geometry.
Removed the second terminal-height reduction and fitted its sign and wall lights to the corrected hall. The human-scale control tower is 24.95 m with fourteen stair flights and a furnished cab.

Preserved the original supplied aircraft design while fitting a continuous opaque cabin frame, separate glazing, a closed flight door, attached live instruments and walkable seats. Fixed local-coordinate clipping/cache errors in ordinary career aircraft as well as physical pilot mode.

Corrected career, heading and map waypoints to the current physical locations and terrain/pavement height. Derive the airspace warning bounds from the complete archipelago so NMC no longer triggers the obsolete boundary warning.

Restored native 3D resolution at both zero and eighty percent pixelation. Pixelation is a final image treatment; geometry, shadows and draw distance are retained. Added world-space soil/moss variation while keeping grass and rock boundaries distinct.

Repaired taxi collision sources: paint, light batches, weather particles and wakes are non-solid; moving boats and airport service parts use stable live geometry rather than stale render-batch transforms; removed-source colliders are retired safely. Real structures and a positive visible-barrier contact remain solid.

Accelerated flight terrain checks with a conservative maximum over every grid cell beneath the airframe, and reject empty swept collision bounds before issuing triangle rays. Corrected physical livestock walking speed/fence spacing and limited neighbour searches to each island herd.

Grouped 2,430 unchanged parked-wheel instances into shared submissions, retaining meshes, materials, shadows and transforms. Preserve CPU instance poses for collision and avoid shortening visibility when grouping parts.

Rebuilt New Mason County for flight-height views: 56 terrain-following paved urban blocks, 10.4–14.4 m core streets, tighter street-facing commercial frontages, larger 28 m commercial footprints and a varied central skyline. Corrected metre/layout mismatches in lot envelopes, setbacks, street clearance and footing samples. Grass in the urban core is now reserved for deliberate pocket parks; docks, rail corridors and outlying farms remain connected. Consolidated pasture fence pieces by their original materials to reduce submissions while retaining the same geometry and shadows.

Calibrated the archipelago to an explicit metre/layout contract: land, terrain and water gaps expand fourfold while the actual 1.7526 m rigged civilian player and the three 192 m harbour cargo-ship hulls keep their physical dimensions. Mason County now spans about 2.10 × 1.45 km, New Mason County about 2.54 × 1.96 km, and the main runway is 872 m long. Relative island arrangement is retained without overlaps.

Separated infrastructure dimensions from map spacing. Roads retain appropriate two-way widths, cars/buses/trucks use class-specific physical widths, rail gauge and 8.8 m track centres stay physical, and 40-foot containers retain their ISO envelopes. Stations, coaches, couplers, boarding routes, ports, parked fleets, ground-service wheel contact and founded connections use the same coordinate policy. People, stairs, seats and controls are not enlarged with the map.

Rebuilt the requested original civilian aircraft designs for walkable interiors, retaining their source wings, tail, gear, propellers and visual style. Enlarged airframes have shortened, fitted forebodies instead of the stretched nose or bus-shaped cabin: the single is about 13.74 m long with a 19.58 m span. Continuous floors, headliners, opaque cabin panels, framed individual windows, clear windshields and closed nose/firewall geometry replace broken shell cuts and open gaps. Original source GLBs remain intact. Placed civilian Photo Mode aircraft now use the same enlarged, fully fitted walkable recipe and preserve propeller, control-surface and gear editing.

Fitted full-height cabins with normal-sized captain/copilot and passenger seats, attached dashboard/coaming, all six live primary instruments, radio/engine readouts, physical yokes/pedals/throttle, separated hand grips, cabin lighting, switches and visible ignition on a clear left-panel flange, verified by real fitted-collider rays in all three cabins. Nose-gear animation translation tracks follow the revised forebody. The same first-person pilot can enter, stand/walk inside, sit, start or stop the engine and return to walking while aloft.

Expanded both detailed hangars around the larger aircraft. Hangar 01 has a 26.8 m clear width, 24.8 m doorway and 29.4 m depth, with an 18-tread human-scale staircase and supported 3.75 m crew mezzanine. Roof ribs/lights, rear workspace, equipment, taxi lead-in and external markings match the new structure. The parking and external lead centreline are shared and offset only 0.5 m, correcting twin/regional wing strikes during door transit. All three civilian airframes are checked against the actual hangar triangles, including the full taxi-out sweep.

Fixed interaction holds that could block another key or another target after completion. Release gating belongs to each physical control; focus loss, pause, settings and reset cancel stale progress. Progress uses monotonic elapsed time so render-delta clamping cannot turn a two-second hold into a longer wait. Holding Q after standing cannot immediately sit the pilot down again. The hollow handle marker, 104-pixel leader, outlined Enter aircraft [F] label and centre-out hold fill remain.

Flight Over releases the native mouse for its buttons, and returning to an active pilot recaptures first-person look. Added gentle grounded footfall motion: about 2.5 cm peak-to-peak rise/dip, subtle alternating sway and less than 0.1 degree of roll, damped when aiming and disabled while seated or airborne.

Fixed invalid bridge-car poses caused by a lane offset still using the old road width: off-deck samples could return negative infinity and become NaN transforms. Road poses now remain on the surveyed deck with finite heights. Walking collision rejects nonfinite source transforms before submitting them to physics, with bounded diagnostic reporting.

Fixed retained weather across Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P menu transitions. Reparenting clouds no longer destroys their particle programs/meshes; fullscreen storm rendering unprojects near/far points correctly for both perspective and orthographic cameras. Underwater environment ownership is released on transfer, and water reflection/clipping uses the new physical sea datum.

Converted flight movement, altitude, wind, camera/terrain queries, map projection, ATC mouse waypoints and collision boundaries to the explicit frame. Uniform layout scaling preserves orthonormal pitch/yaw/roll instead of shearing a banked cabin. Removed spawn-time scale resets that could enlarge aircraft and people fourfold after boarding. Weather sampling converts physical observer positions to layout cells while rain stays around the physical camera. Expanded Dogfight/Convoy bounds, objective transforms, jet spawn terrain clearance and collision altitude gates use the calibrated world. Retained-world public traffic is seeded in the final frame to avoid duplicate road positions.

Kept the temporary Cmd+Shift+P / Ctrl+Shift+P entry from the main menu and station picker: WASD/mouse, Shift run, Ctrl crouch and Space jump; hold F for 2 seconds at the door and Q for 0.5 seconds at the captain chair. Hold E at ignition to crank, then release before E/Q throttle; C cycles chase/close/cockpit. P pauses, O opens settings, Escape closes settings first and R restores the cold aircraft in Hangar 01. No career job or progression is awarded.

Genuinely regenerated the construction geometry for the calibrated world and denser NMC. Removed 8,289 obsolete generated caches across 5 nonempty cleanup stages identified by complete bakes and recursive resource-dependency inventories, removing 95,625,664 cumulative logical file bytes. The final cache contains 7,755 active resources; its expanded-world/city geometry is 62,399,835 bytes larger than the previous saved BR cache, so cumulative deletion is not net update storage savings. Player data, raw source models and all 26 authentic historical Alpha archives are preserved. Public launch/countdown remains November 21, 2026, 4:30 PM CST.

Closed the cabin-to-tail seam on both sides of all three civilian airframes, corrected the generated shell face normals, removed disconnected decorative cap fragments and retained the connected original tail paint. Opaque hull panels and doors remain separate from actual glazing, with two-sided shadow casting for the shell. Exterior reviews include banked, underside, front, rear, wing-join and side views, with complete surface-depth and face-normal checks.

Optimized rail lane sampling and shared coach-body sway while preserving measured route poses, buffer/coupler bounds, boarding states and schedules. Coupler barrels, working gangway floors and spring motion remain physical. Live civilian instrument panels skip redraws for identical instrument input states; placed Photo Mode panels render once, while changing flight values still update.

Corrected ATC radio conflict-altitude conversion and tower radar coordinates for the calibrated four-metres-per-layout-unit frame. Same-altitude and separated-flight alerts use actual feet, forecast distances report nautical miles and the tower outer range ring is labeled 3.2 NM.

Cached fixed primary-instrument and power-quadrant artwork in a twice-resolution one-shot atlas, retaining the existing full-rate live needles, attitude, heading cards and numerical readings. Identical supplied states skip redundant redraw requests. Resize, jet scale/configuration, theme and font-resource changes invalidate the cache, and instruments remain click-through. Native artwork and 120-frame live-update checks plus the actual dogfight spectator telemetry gate verify the shared HUD path.

Fixed distant city buildings disappearing after the fourfold world calibration: semantic architecture is reserved for structural spatial/material batching before generic scenery batching can assign short distance cutoffs. Complete building silhouettes remain visible in overview views with mesh LODs, while exact static shadow geometry remains consolidated.

Removed mathematically dead ocean shader work without changing the wave, fade, absorption, refraction or reflection equations: skip noise at existing exactly-zero weights, share repeated warp/distance calculations and avoid reconstructing depth samples already rejected by the existing condition. Four fixed-time native views show no visible change; measured GPU rounding is at most 2/255 per channel with worst mean below 0.005/255.

Corrected remaining station and earthwork unit conversions found in actual close-ups. Name boards embed into their hall facades, lettering clears the backing, number plates attach to poles and door handles attach to doors. The rail formation now sits 25 cm below the rail datum instead of one metre, supporting ballast and platform undersides while preserving route, consist and road-crossing equations.

Validated the corrected source in eight focused, unpaused native Apple M4/Metal gameplay views at 1280 × 800 with shaders enabled: 53.47–155.29 average FPS, saved 27% and default 80% pixelation. All eight exceed the 50 average-FPS gate; occasional slower frames remain and the soft 58+ target is not met in every view. The final six-cycle real-key spawn/board/seat/ignition/reset/storm-menu regression passes 99/99 checks across 27 screenshots with unchanged runtime/geometry fingerprints. No new native app or EXE is packaged.

Clipped individual rain streaks inside fitted hangar roofs, the octagonal ATC tower and the moving/banked civilian cabin. Outdoor rain stays visible through open doors and glazing; all 1,800 instances remain active. Cached roof transforms update after retained-world reparenting, and paused Photo Mode initializes shelter uniforms immediately. Geometry/lifecycle and five paired native views verify sheltering without hiding the whole rain field.

Corrected the right-wall tool bench/shelf orientation in both airport hangars so the tools face into the room instead of toward the wall. Both hangars retain their detailed interiors, mezzanines and stairs.

Replaced the three solid control-tower primitives with a complete four-level regional tower: ground entrance/lobby, technical services, crew facilities and an octagonal glazed cab. The tower remains at the existing terminal-side location; its slightly wider cab, roof fittings and obstruction beacon are fitted to the new structure.

Added a real entrance opening, framed glazed hinged door, handles, kick plates, access reader, entrance canopy/light and crew signage. The door exposes open/closed interaction state with matching rotated collision and starts open for the current spectator workflow.

Built six switchback stair flights with 54 treads, supported intermediate landings, stringers, handrails, guardrails, safety nosings, stair lighting and a continuous physical route to the cab. Upper slabs retain actual stair openings and fitted ramp collisions prepare future character movement.

Added three furnished controller positions plus a supervisor desk, seven deep CRT housings, fifteen physical strip holders, nine radio/voice modules, microphones, headsets, keyboards, mice, foot pedals, binoculars and a supported signal-light gun. Cab consoles are kept below seated sightlines, with clear outward-sloping glazing, shade rollers, acoustic ceiling panels and ventilation details.

Tower CRTs share one nearby-only 1024-square instrument atlas that refreshes at a bounded rate. Radar returns, flight strips, wind and operational readouts bind to actual airport traffic; the atlas stops updating at a distance and does not advance paused traffic simulation.

Furnished the technical floor with three detailed racks containing 33 equipment modules, patching, UPS/battery units and bracketed cable routes. The lobby has lockers, an entry directory, phone, radiator and first-aid/fire points. The crew floor has briefing/chart space, reference binders, seating, coffee equipment, cups, a shift board and a compact modeled washroom.

Downloaded eight selected CC0 Furniture Kit models by Kenney and combined their original geometry/material colours into compact resources with distance LODs. Per-file/source ZIP SHA-256 values, the original license and credits are included; the complete source pack is organized under asset_sources rather than the project root.

Grouped tower architecture and small fittings by material, range-limited interior props/screens and lights, and rebuilt the affected construction-layer and aggregate cache resources. Detailed tower interiors and furniture collisions prepare the walkable expansion; the November 11 temporary walking/boarding route now builds on this work; seated console interaction remains planned.

Static batching now respects runtime-exclusion metadata through an object ancestry chain. Live viewport-backed tower CRTs and hinged door geometry/shadows remain owned by their runtime objects instead of being serialized into immutable construction recipes.

Bound the 3D rendering budget against native window and logical canvas dimensions, with deferred resize updates and an actual-image size probe. This preserves the normal-window resolution, native interface and full-resolution cinematic Photo Mode.

Removed the estimated-completion bar from every dogfight matchmaking stage: finding a server, connecting/loading, match found and finding players. Text elapsed-time counters, portrait fades, actual roster counts and retry/back controls remain; the real world-construction preview retains its genuine build progress.

Dogfight deployments now rotate across the full 360-degree arena with radius, altitude and heading variation. Consecutive matches cannot reuse the previous deployment sector. Online and offline share the same deployment code and retain unique combat identities and safe spacing.

Spectator HUDs now bind health, primary flight instruments, throttle, engine N1/EGT, armament, lock/reticle, radar, threat warnings and cockpit symbology to the observed aircraft. Aircraft switching, target destruction, leaving spectator and new rounds rebind correctly without transferring player control.

Added per-pilot kill/streak histories for spectator Battle Royale data and winner statistics. Engine spool, temperature and vibration clocks now belong to each airframe, eliminating inherited engine readings when changing observed pilots. G readings use the airframe load calculation.

Moved spectator controls to the upper centre so they no longer cover the radar. Camera cycling is available while spectating, and the former hull-intersecting close camera is replaced by a clear high-shoulder view.

Rebuilt pilot-view interiors for F-15, MiG-29 and Rafale with fitted structure, curved canopy framing, ejection seats/harnesses, coaming, side consoles, switches, animated stick/throttle, HUD glass and live physical instrument screens. The MiG adds round instruments and a turquoise panel; Rafale uses a side-stick and lower canopy profile.

Pilot view now uses dedicated cockpit geometry and hides that aircraft exterior mesh, restoring it when changing camera or subject. A lowered viewing angle and revised FOV keep the outside view and complete instrument panel visible. Cockpits are allocated only when used; inactive instrument viewports stop rendering.

Replaced both solid airport hangar boxes with open-front, grounded buildings, structural frames/trusses, skylights, retracted door tracks, slab joints, mezzanines and human-scale staircases (Hangar 01 now has eighteen treads). The ATC-side building at local x=43 is Hangar 01 / Pilot Services; the edge building is Hangar 02 / Engineering.

Furnished hangars with crew briefing tables, charts, CRT workstations or parts planning, chairs, benches, tool boards, cabinets, drawer trolleys, jacks, oxygen bottles, compressor, hose reel, fire points, safety markings, cable trays and interior work lighting. Floors, platforms, supports, stair ramps and mezzanine guardrails have collision for later walking development.

Merged authored small details into material-grouped meshes, range-limited hangar fittings and lights, and refreshed the affected construction caches. These interiors prepare the planned walkable hub; the November 11 temporary walking/boarding route now builds on these interiors; interactive computer mode remains planned.

Fixed a missile validity error when its target has already been freed. Existing yellow-acquisition guidance, pause/settings ownership and contracted private-study release requirements remain in force.

Rebuilt minigame routing and matchmaking as a coherent CL-95 desktop application, with shared sunset wallpaper, a taskbar, window chrome, breadcrumbs, cream route cards and Cloudline artwork. Matchmaking dialogs size to their contents, eliminating the oversized gap below Back.

Fixed online/offline Back buttons being covered by full-screen layout containers. Back, close and Escape now follow one-level navigation; aircraft selection also has a Back action. Native pointer-hit tests cover the actual route controls.

Replaced the illustrated queue faces with twenty real photographic portraits whose individual Wikimedia Commons records identify CC0 publication from Unsplash before June 2017. High-resolution originals are locally bundled and framed with non-destructive texture regions; three-second portrait cycling and crossfades remain.

Finding players now begins at an independently randomized 0–26 found count, then advances monotonically to the actual roster. Short-lobby and non-ready-player removals remain bounded by the existing five-slot combined limit.

Moved P/O/Escape ownership from per-frame key polling to handled input events. P freezes aircraft, camera, combat, background trains and world processing; O opens settings with the same freeze. Escape closes settings without exiting the match, and closing settings restores the prior paused/running state. Deployment countdowns also obey pause.

Aircraft missiles and the Convoy Strike ground launcher can fire while a yellow target is still acquiring. Early shots have up to 0.45 seconds of initial straight flight and reduced turn authority; red/full lock gives immediate full guidance. Existing ammunition, cooldown, target validity and pause restrictions remain.

Updated the contracted private study interface to use neutral online labels throughout its menus, loading, aircraft selection and HUD. The implementation remains local AI: source comments and development documentation require real multiplayer or restored simulation disclosure before public distribution. No app/EXE distribution was packaged.

Added a phased walkable-airport hub plan: start at a CL-95 workstation, run minigame selection inside its desktop, leave the computer to walk to aircraft or the tower, reuse one persistent world, and preserve optional quick resume. The November 11 temporary Hangar 01 walking/boarding route now provides the first physical prototype; the full desktop hub remains planned.

CL-95 revision verification passed 20,000 session draws, 56 native UI/roster checks, 10 missile-acquisition checks and live P/O/Escape tests with frozen aircraft/camera/background trains. The 30-pilot dogfight averaged 60.01 FPS. Eight focused current-source Apple M4 gameplay views at 1280×800 with shaders on averaged 59.88–122.47 FPS, including storm views at the saved 27% pixelation setting. These are bounded ten-second observations, not an every-frame or packaged/Windows guarantee.

Added Online and Offline minigame menus with an Online Dogfighting route. The current interface is the contracted private study version; development documentation describes its local implementation and release requirements.

Simulated dogfight rosters use unique Player001–Player030 aliases, with the human assigned a random unused ID. Internal combat ownership stays unchanged. Offline dogfight and Convoy Strike use Player001 for the human and numbered AI aliases for both teams, including role swaps and ground-defense kills.

The local matchmaking experiment includes 1–19-second server searches weighted toward 6–9 seconds, a three-second Match Found hold, 2–7-second loading weighted toward 4–5 seconds, and 4–17-second player discovery with a live found counter. Monotonic elapsed clocks keep queue and ready timers independent of simulation time.

Server-finding failures occur with an independent 8% probability and loading failures with 14%; failed queues require explicit retry, reset elapsed time and reshuffle avatars. Back or the window close button cancels the queue without launching a delayed match.

The initial illustrated-avatar queue was replaced by twenty CC0 photographic portraits in the subsequent CL-95 visual revision. Source pages, photographer credits, download URLs and hashes are preserved with the photographic assets.

Player discovery starts at a randomized 0–26 found count and has a 7% short-lobby chance, missing one to three opponents with a strong one-to-two bias. The aircraft screen retains a 60-second Ready Up deadline, live ready count and occasional non-ready roster slots.

Ready checks begin only after the actual game world and aircraft picker are visible. All-ready lobbies start the normal five-second deployment countdown immediately; at the deadline only non-ready bots are removed. An unready human returns to the Online menu. The combined shortfall is capped at five pilots. Pause and settings hold the ready clock and deployment countdown.

Aircraft selection remains immediate offline. Online aircraft cards select without deploying; Ready Up locks the selected aircraft. Simulated-online wins, losses and streaks do not award persistent profile progress.

Kill feed, eliminated, spectator and winner displays use the assigned aliases. Bot winners are now announced, including a human eliminated in the final pair. Aircraft swaps and new rounds refresh cached live-fighter references to prevent freed-object reticle errors.

Workspace cleanup removed 644 duplicate, superseded or regenerable files totaling 116,342,733 file bytes (116.34 MB). Twelve unique source-pack ZIPs totaling 170,965,494 bytes were organized under asset_sources/3d_assets/source_packs. Active game model payloads and all 26 historical Alpha release ZIPs were preserved; source import tooling now follows the organized source paths.

November 10 matchmaking revision verification: 20,000 seeded session draws and rendered flow checks passed, including retries, cancellation, short rosters and winner aliases. A real 30-pilot native dogfight averaged 59.98 FPS, and eight focused current-source Apple M4 Mobile/Metal gameplay views averaged 59.67–60.10 FPS at 1280×800 with shaders on. These are bounded ten-second observations, not an every-frame or Windows/distribution guarantee; earlier dated FPS entries describe their own prior passes.

November 10 farm correction: removed the long artificial ridge beside the MC barns and rebuilt the three affected static construction recipes. The farm now joins the surrounding ground without the added hill.

Rebuilt overcast and storm coverage as a depth-aware three-dimensional cloud volume spanning the archipelago: a rolling nimbostratus ceiling, taller convective forms and a separate upper altostratus layer share wind, sun scattering and internal lightning illumination. Clouds remain visible above the sea and in Photo Mode water reflections.

Rain and thunderstorms now combine a continuous distant precipitation curtain with up to 1,800 finer nearby rain streaks in a concentrated observer-centered volume. GPU-instanced streaks follow the active camera without per-drop CPU transform uploads. § OVERVIEW

BR-1.0.0 'The Living Archipelago' is the biggest Cloudline release to date — it turns Mason County and its outlying islands from scenery into a working region you earn a career in, with a tower that talks you through every flight, paper contracts you physically sign, and an economy that reacts to what you fly where.

§ THE LIVING ARCHIPELAGO — THE WORLD

Every destination is an authored place rather than generic island scenery: Juniper Reach, Skylark, Gullhaven, Granite Point, Northwatch, Beacon Harbor, Port Halcyon, Meadowmere, Sanctuary Bay, Lookout Cove, Tidepool Landing and Harbor Point each have a named town, an economic district, a marina, an emergency facility, an airfield and an offshore port anchor.

Each island carries its own role and identity — farming, forestry, quarrying, weather station, lighthouse, fishing cove, wildflower meadows, bird sanctuary, lookout, tidepools and harbor — which shapes its buildings, land use and the cargo it needs.

Road-locked scheduled ground traffic brings the towns to life: cars, cargo trucks, buses, emergency vehicles, residents and terminal travelers follow explicit town-to-terminal-to-worksite-to-marina anchor chains and yield in lane instead of being shoved off the road.

Scheduled marine traffic runs on validated routes — ferries, fishing boats and a cargo barge with proper hull variants, wakes, operating hours and port metadata — and no water route is ever created unless every segment clears the island coastlines.
Daily construction closures visibly drop barriers and hold cargo traffic, and dent local satisfaction while they are active.

Weather or an explicit isolation state can suspend an island's air service, hold its commuter legs, grow its unmet demand, and update the tower's live island-accessibility board so you can see which fields are open.
The strategic island-overview camera was reframed and the animated ocean and seabed were expanded well past the view bounds so the map can never expose an ocean edge.
§ THE TRANSPORT CAREER — THE JOB
Cockpit mode is now a full airline job rather than a sandbox: you are dispatched real work, flown start to finish under tower control.

The tower talks you through the entire flight — clearance, taxi, hold short, cleared for takeoff, departure, enroute, approach, cleared to land, taxi to stand, and offload — with each instruction shown in a readable band and logged to a comms history.
A glowing, mitered route ribbon lights the exact taxi and routing path directly on the pavement, so you always know where to go on the ground.
Numbered 1-to-N waypoints drop in the world and on the map in order and tick off as you reach them, replacing guesswork with a clear route to fly.

Missions are procedurally generated and weather-aware: the active runway follows the wind, dirt strips close in rain, and payload weight feeds the takeoff model, so the combinations are effectively endless.
Multi-island chains string several legs together with a chain bonus, and a standing-contracts layer (Supply Run, Lifelines, Grand Tour and more) tracks long-term goals across many flights.
§ SIGNABLE PAPER CONTRACTS

Every accepted job is a readable paper charter you must actually read and sign before it begins — headed CONTRACT #N (your lifetime completed count), it names a real client drawn from the destination town's economy (its marina, district, facility or council) with that counterparty's signature already on the page.

The charter lists the consignment, the full leg-by-leg routing, the delivery window, the consideration (Advancement Points plus Flight Credits), and four to five generated terms and conditions, so combined with the procedural routing the contract text is effectively never repeated.
At the bottom is a SIGN HERE box: click it, type your aircraft's tail number, and SIGN & ACCEPT to start the job — or request a different charter instead.

Ultra-rare charters (about 5%) are issued by the Office of the Territorial Governor on sealed-blue official stock rather than the usual parchment, carry a confidential 'sealed' clause and a much larger payout, and unlock a hidden achievement.
Signing your first contract unlocks the 'Ink on Paper' achievement.
