§ ATC & NAVIGATION — RULES THAT ENFORCE

The flight lifecycle is strict and actually checked: route waypoints are consumed in order (reaching a later one early does nothing), you must stop and HOLD SHORT and wait before a takeoff clearance is issued, and entering the runway before you are cleared is a logged incursion.
Departing without a clearance, departing on the wrong runway or heading (more than 55 degrees off), or landing at a field you were not cleared for are all detected violations.
Departure detection is latched so it fires exactly once per leg on first lift-off, instead of relying on a single frame that could be missed — so these violations are caught reliably.
Every violation records an ATC reprimand, applies an Advancement-Point and reputation penalty, and shows an unmistakable red on-screen notice.
The tower now reads a real computed heading on departure ('fly heading 073 direct BKN') and the correct runway heading on approach.

Enroute fixes are generated densely along each leg (roughly every 420 m) as lit floor beacons — a spreading pulse pad with a vertical beam — so the path to fly is always visible, and island arrivals get a clear lit taxi path from the runway to the stand.
The Journey Map draws three lines at once: blue to the island, green to your next mission waypoint, and magenta to your own placed waypoint.
§ THE ECONOMY — DELIVERIES THAT MATTER
Every island carries a real, lazily-accruing transport demand, seeded per island and growing over time — faster for weathered, unpaved strips that rely more on air service.
Completing a delivery writes the units back and drops that island's backlog, so your flying actually changes the regional picture.
The mission generator weights destinations by demand and applies surge pricing, so a starved, high-demand field can pay up to 1.8 times the base.
The aircraft inspector surfaces each flight's regional cargo and passenger outcome so you can see the effect of a delivery.
§ FLIGHT MODEL — EARN THE LIFT
Automatic takeoff is gone: lift-off is solely a pilot action — hold the rotation input at or above the 62-knot rotation speed on a usable runway.
A sustained-climb contract keeps your commanded power and pitch through the first rotation transition, giving the wing time to build lift instead of dropping straight back onto the runway.

Takeoff is a multi-factor model: flap setting, head/tailwind (a headwind shortens the roll, a tailwind lengthens it), crosswind (the airframe weathercocks and drifts and must be held with rudder), engine RPM and spool state, and an over-rotation penalty that drags the tail if you haul the nose up too early.

The rudder is a genuine aerodynamic control: the pedals command sideslip, the nose swings off the flight path, a side force gradually curves the track, dihedral rolls the aircraft, sideslip costs drag, and holding uncoordinated rudder near the stall departs the wing.
The departure runway is chosen for where you are going, balancing headwind against pointing toward your destination (a strong wind still wins for safety).

The analog propeller gauge was rebuilt so its pointer, tick labels, operating arcs and digital readout share one literal 0-5,000 RPM scale with a smooth fixed-pitch response, replacing the old linear ramp and yellow-range wall.

A runway-only rotation-assist exists purely as an input-safety net if a platform drops the held pitch-up event with takeoff power established; manual rotation always commits immediately at Vr, and grass, apron, taxiway and unusable dirt are never auto-rotated.
§ AIRCRAFT & THE FLEET
Three airframes are in the fleet: the CL-150 Skylark to start, the CL-310 Twin Courier unlocked at Commercial rank, and the CL-600 Regional turboprop unlocked at ATP.
The cockpit spawns your selected airframe and the per-profile flight model (size, engines, wake) makes it genuinely fly as the bigger aircraft.

Other aircraft's propellers now always spin about each blade disc's correct axis, with a visible idle windmill that scales with delivered power, so wing-mounted turboprop discs animate like the nose tractor prop.
§ PROGRESSION — RANKS & ADVANCEMENT POINTS
A persistent player profile is saved as JSON in a shared Cloudline user directory and tracks your whole career across sessions.

It records lifetime stats — minutes airborne, flights, takeoffs, landings, greasers, night landings, islands visited, crashes, tower shifts, flight credits and more — plus Advancement Points, Flight Credits, a 0-100 reputation, and ATC reprimands.
A shared rank ladder runs Student, Private, Commercial, ATP, Chief, and you climb it by flying — landings and tower shifts award Advancement Points, and promotions fire in-game toasts.
Reputation rises with clean, on-time, careful delivery and falls with crashes, disregarded ATC and damaged goods.
§ ACHIEVEMENTS — 50 TO EARN

The achievement roster expanded to 50 (up from the earlier set), driven by a data-driven engine that hooks into real landing, crash, takeoff, airborne-time, island, night, day-cycle, tower-shift, contract and delivery events.

They include contract-count tiers, contract-signing tiers, leg-courier tiers, Flight-Credit milestones (Flush, Air Tycoon), per-service-type badges (People Mover, Surge Hauler, Freight Dog), the on-time Metronome, a well-travelled badge, the near-miss Close Call, the first-failure Lesson Learned, a 25-landing Silver Wings, the triple-hop chain, 'Ink on Paper' for your first signature, and the hidden 'Classified Charter' for a governor's contract.
Unlocks and promotions surface as in-game toasts so you see progress as you fly.
§ TIME-SENSITIVE DELIVERY & THE LOOT TABLE

Deliveries are time-sensitive: each leg's Advancement Points and Flight Credits scale with how much of the delivery window is left, up to 2x when you arrive with plenty of time to spare, on top of cargo condition and any active multiplier.
Finishing a contract with 40% or more of the window remaining rolls a weighted comfort-bonus loot table (Common through Legendary, roughly a 49/29/15/5/2 percent split).

Loot prizes include Flight Credits, Advancement Points, reputation, a 1.25x-2x next-contract multiplier, a Rare Dispatch Shuffle Token (an extra board shuffle), an Ultra-Rare Open Skies Pass (free-flight access), and a Legendary new airframe.
§ FREE FLIGHT — THE SKYRING CIRCUIT

Free Flight is the Skyring circuit: a loop of eight upright hoops in the air over Mason County that you take off and fly through in order, scored by rings and time, paying Advancement Points and Flight Credits on completion.
Free Flight is gated behind Commercial rank and shown clearly locked until you reach it.
The ENTER screen is now three stations — Flight Deck, Air Traffic, and Open Skies / Free Flight — with the third locked until Commercial.
§ AI TRAFFIC

AI traffic aircraft were completely revamped: departures line up on the runway centerline in one smooth curve and climb out straight on the runway heading, instead of the old turn-off-then-back-on lineup.

Arrivals that must wait fly a real holding racetrack — two straight legs joined by 180-degree turns — each on its own altitude layer and phase, so holding traffic disperses around an oval instead of stacking in a column over the tower.
Separation is mode-aware: in Cockpit mode the AI flies and separates itself, while in Tower mode the last-moment behaviour is kept so conflicts the controller creates must be resolved by the human.
AI right-of-way holds each aircraft at its exact current pose, so there is no player-conflict displacement anywhere in the traffic stack.
§ GROUND OPERATIONS & SERVICE
Airport life runs at a believable operational density — travelers, ramp crew, public and parking-road cars, a bus, parked cars and baggage tugs — all scaled against the measured player airframe.

Fuel, stairs, catering, operations and baggage equipment stay staged until a parked aircraft requests service, drive to that aircraft, remain for the job, and return to their assigned stand instead of endlessly circling the apron.
Gate 5 is a protected player stand: ground operations never dispatch service work to the pilot-controlled aircraft, and active vehicles yield outside an 18-unit protected radius.

At normal taxi speed a vehicle or aircraft contact becomes a stopped, separated ground conflict with a clear warning instead of an instant flight-ending crash; high-energy runway impacts and airborne collisions remain consequential.
§ CRASH, IMPACT & DITCHING PHYSICS

Severity-based impact handling covers terrain, runways, buildings, aircraft, ground vehicles, vessels and water: relative velocity, impact attitude, object scale and surface type determine debris, flash and fire, smoke, spray, reciprocal aircraft damage, and controlled-versus-destructive ditching.

Every effect uses bounded low-poly geometry for stable performance — a single emissive pixel burst, one faceted flash, and at most a few low-poly smoke puffs — with no cone flames or stray flying-debris nodes.

Aircraft-to-aircraft impacts use a reciprocal two-body momentum response; runway collisions send both aircraft into speed-sensitive skids with wet-surface braking, and airborne collisions preserve the remaining motion, rotation and gravity-driven fall instead of freezing either airframe.

A player-ending impact transitions directly into an input-locked, monochrome live aftermath: the crash physics, explosion, smoke, skid or fall keep progressing in real time with no reset, pause, settings, camera or exit controls, then present Flight Over with Gate 5 respawn and airport-menu choices.
Crash-grounding is rebuilt around the measured aircraft bounds so wings, nose, tail, wheels and model corners stay above the actual terrain while a damaged aircraft skids or settles.

In the transport job, a crash fails the active contract permanently (you can never draw that same contract again), applies a severe penalty scaled by impact severity, and draws a fresh charter on respawn.

Flight-obstacle hitboxes were calibrated to the visible structures — the radio mast, wind-turbine mast and rotor disc, control tower, trees and cabins — so flying near a thin structure no longer counts as a strike while genuine strikes still register.
§ WEATHER & ATMOSPHERE

Visual fog, rain, wind and storm lighting ease across a moving cell edge, while navigation, radar and aircraft weather sampling still receive the exact local cell data as the visible air mass builds and clears.

Regional weather drives gameplay: runway-in-use follows the wind, dirt strips close in rain, and steady wind changes ground track and speed while gust deltas change indicated airflow, slip and aircraft response.
§ THE COCKPIT HUD

The cockpit and tower HUDs share one consistent Windows-95 panel language — grey bevelled panels, dark readable text, period buttons, dropdowns and input fields — including the decision and MAYDAY queue and the command terminal.
Air data labels indicated airspeed as KIAS, reports ground speed as GS separately, and shows signed HEAD and XWIND wind components.

The cockpit's top job strip is a compact, centered Win95-grey mini-bar that matches the instrument panel, and the current-instruction band is centered at the bottom between the left and right HUD blocks.
A red STALL takeover cue overrides the band when the wing is stalled.
§ THE JOURNEY MAP

A draggable Windows-95 Journey Map (press J) renders the live 3D world top-down — real terrain, water, runways, buildings and live aircraft — through a SubViewport that shares the game's World3D with an orthographic camera.

It opens heading-up centered on the aircraft, then expands to a north-up pan/zoom whole-archipelago view, and closes on a third press; right-click drops a world waypoint drawn as a tall vertical marker that clears once you fly within range.

The map uses its own clear, fog-free environment so it reads in any weather, and the planned route, waypoints and the player triangle (orange on the ground, cyan in the air) are projected through the same camera so they sit exactly on the real runways at any zoom or rotation.
§ THE PILOT LOGBOOK
The career screen moved from the launcher into the game (main menu, PILOT LOGBOOK) and was rebuilt in the game's Windows-95 window style.

It shows your rank with an Advancement-Point progress bar to the next rank, a full lifetime-stats grid, your fleet, and the complete 50-achievement list marked unlocked or locked, across CAREER FILE, HANGAR and SERVICE RECORD tabs — including ATC reprimands, contracts failed and near-misses.
§ PRESENTATION & RETRO TREATMENTS

Display & Visuals now uses one adjustable Pixel Classic presentation, enhanced Shaders on by default, and optional matching HUD/UI and native cursor treatment. Photo mode has its own separate cinematic renderer. Earlier Alpha presentation modes remain in historical notes; they are not choices in this BR build.

The world loads behind a bordered, 1995-style progress window. Terrain and imported buildings appear in layers during close island views, then the ocean and archipelago come into view. The progress bar and adaptive numeric time estimate follow actual work.
The menu hero loop opens mid-action on short final and moves the wide archipelago establishing shot to last, so it reads as a live, dynamic scene.
§ THE LAUNCHER

The launcher is a self-contained Windows-95 desktop application — a teal desktop behind one grey bevelled window with a navy caption bar and working minimize, maximize and close buttons — matching the game's in-cockpit chrome.
It fingerprints every extracted source snapshot, so a rebuilt same-version BR-1.0.0 release is re-extracted automatically on the next PLAY instead of launching stale code.

The OVERVIEW page shows a live launch countdown, the PLAY page is a full launch station with the version list and developer-clearance field, PATCH NOTES holds the complete flight record, EXTRAS carries the wallpaper export, and SETTINGS configures the launchpad.
Every screen was reworked for readability: dark text on the grey face, navy section accents, a clearly-marked selected tab, and a readable Danger Zone.
§ LIVE WALLPAPER EXPORT

Extras includes Live Wallpaper Export: a 32-second, HUD-free menu-world loop plus a matching still, rendered directly from the real menu scene rather than screen-recorded, so the island overview, runway approach, terminal apron, landside cameras, traffic, boats, clouds and water are the only things in the file.

One action writes both files to Documents/Cloudline Wallpapers and opens the folder; Windows can apply the loop through Lively Wallpaper when installed, and macOS receives the native-ready still plus an MP4 for a separate live-wallpaper or screensaver app, with version-aware setup guidance.
Preview Clean Live World remains available as the borderless live renderer, exiting with Esc or Q.
§ PLAYER DATA & SETTINGS

Settings ends with a Danger Zone holding Export Player Data (a timestamped JSON copy in the actual Cloudline data folder beside the live player file) and Delete Player Data. Delete requires typing CLOUDLINE; export preserves the live save.
Each destructive action opens a confirmation that requires typing CLOUDLINE before it will proceed.
A startup-destination setting lets you choose which launcher page opens first, and preferences are stored locally on the device.
§ STABILITY, PERFORMANCE & VERIFICATION

Every drop in this cycle was verified on Godot 4.7.2 with a clean full-project parse and compile, plus dedicated headless harnesses exercising the contract generator and sign flow, the penalty/reputation/achievement APIs, demand accrual and write-back, surge pricing, the mission board, island taxi routing, the 50-achievement roster, the fleet unlocks and the Free-Flight rank gate.

Full-loop regression tests drive takeoff climb-out and short-final landings through the exact per-frame flight and obstacle pass the live game runs, including a no-auto-takeoff assertion that a full-power roll past Vr stays on the ground until the pilot rotates.

Exact collision sampling is capped at a safe rate, caches active ground vehicles, and broad-rejects distant aircraft and vehicles before detailed probes, to keep a high frame rate without removing collision coverage.
§ DEVELOPER-BUILD NOTES
BR-1.0.0 is public and playable directly from the launcher. It remains a separate bundled snapshot, so edits to the working tree cannot silently change an earlier catalog version.

On Mac and Windows, launcher PLAY installs the fingerprinted BR source snapshot and its matching compiled native game, then starts that compiled game. The source archive remains complete for verification and fallback. A rebuilt same-version package changes its SHA-256, so the launcher replaces stale installed bytes on the next PLAY without a version bump.
Mouse flight aim now spans the game window and gains tiny movement-only response variations for a more tactile aircraft feel.

Convoy Strike joins the minigames as the second card. Fifteen attackers face fifteen defenders over four random islands carrying 50–100 vehicles each. Attackers must destroy every envoy before the 15-minute clock; defenders win if any survive.

The convoy fleet uses SIpriv CC BY 4.0 BTR 82, Gepard, Humvee, BM 30 Smerch, S300, and parked SU-37 models. Radar and launcher variants use their authored animations or deployment poses. Gepards and S300s launch unlimited missiles with a 25–30-second cooldown.

All three fighters carry bombs with different strike strengths. Press V in keyboard flight or right click in mouse flight; a bomb returns every 15 seconds, and a final envoy kill immediately grants one. The HUD shows a predicted impact marker, island health bar, fleet count, 15-minute timer, team colors, and friendly lock protection. Aircraft and defenders respawn during the match.
Mouse flight now responds more strongly as the aim ring approaches a window corner, with precise control near the centre.

The Convoy Strike mission window now shows live target count, island health, team strength, bomb pips, and recharge progress. The mission timer uses an outlined face without the old rectangular backing.

Convoy Strike now keeps aircraft inside the finite rendered world. A warning area starts well before the ocean edge, and a hard boundary resolves through the normal death and respawn flow. Battle Royale boundary rendering also skips close-up stripe shading to avoid a full-screen slowdown.

The Convoy Strike mission board now matches the gray Windows 95 armament panel while retaining its island, team, and bomb readouts. Ground-to-air missile cooldown varies from 30 seconds with a full defense network toward 25 seconds as launchers are destroyed; opening shots are staggered.

Convoy Strike now has 15 attackers and 15 defenders. Respawns reuse each fighter's imported model instead of rebuilding it during combat. The shared kill feed now detaches rows before deferred deletion, fixing an infinite loop that could freeze or crash after several kills. Distance fog hides the finite map edge at high altitude in both minigames.

Mouse flight now uses continuous relative input, with hidden capture restored immediately after respawn. Ground launchers still have 25–30-second individual cooldowns, but their network spaces launches at least five seconds apart, limits simultaneous missiles, and sends only one at a time toward each jet. Their shorter engagement range gives attackers room to approach.
The aircraft picker remains hidden through the final loading frames and appears only after the loading cover has fully faded away in Battle Royale and Convoy Strike.

The Living Archipelago now uses 24 individual Creative Mango road vehicles, including a rare F1 car, with animated tire meshes. Traffic follows island grades and Mason County's real sloped tunnel portals; camper trailers are omitted. Island road links, the terminal's east return road, and Sanctuary Island's stilted lookout boardwalk are expanded. Creative Mango's CC BY 4.0 attribution appears in the launcher credits.

Convoy Strike now lets the player defend. Choose one of the three fighters with bombing disabled and right-click missile fire, or select an S-300 ground launcher at a random island airfield. Its vehicle camera, air-search scope, timed lock, eight missiles, 15-second launch cooldown, 30-second missile resupply, and bonus missile every two kills make ground defense playable. Holding R for three seconds sacrifices the current unit and reopens the role picker without restarting the match.

Ground S-300 defense has three C-key views: optic, launcher, and tactical. The selected launcher rack follows mouse aim, and every aircraft kill displays +1 KILL even alongside a missile reward. Island houses have rebuilt continuous roofs, gable walls, windows, doors, and varied porch details; the roof panels no longer cut through the walls. Batched house trim keeps island rendering lighter.

November 10 cinematic atmosphere rebuild: sunrise and sunset now follow solar elevation, with a gold horizon, rose/lavender twilight, cooler upper sky and a gradual blue-hour transition. A bounded HDR sun core and layered aureole retain bright sun shots without whitening the whole archipelago.

Unified cinematic world and Photo Mode lighting: warm low-angle sunlight, cooler ambient fill, directional cloud shading and copper/silver cloud rims follow the same solar palette. Photo time/weather controls retain their overrides and restore the original environment on exit.

Reworked the cinematic lens finish with multi-scale highlight diffusion, luminance-masked warm highlights/cool shadows, restrained sun diffraction, an anamorphic streak and additive lens ghosts. Sky precision noise removes packed-HDR night banding without restoring a retro dither treatment.

Fixed cinematic post-processing being erased by the later pixel/CRT pass. An explicit back-buffer copy now composes both passes, preserving the native HUD unless its treatment setting is enabled. The shader switch disables cinematic optics and restores baseline sunlight.

Water now has a tighter enhanced specular response and stronger true Photo Mode reflections, carrying the new sunrise/sunset palette over the swell. Full-resolution Photo Mode retains its separate reflection render; normal gameplay retains the existing single-world rendering approach.

Cinematic rendering verification: five time-of-day captures plus storm and lunar views; shader, weather-fog, moon, UI/cursor and Photo Mode restoration checks passed. Six focused Apple M4 source views averaged 85.37–153.17 FPS at 1280×800, shaders enabled, default 80% and saved 51% pixelation. These bounded averages are not Windows, long-session or guaranteed minimum-frame results.

Decoupled the reusable ATC tower from game/menu scene classes so standalone model tools and headless fixtures load without pulling in gameplay autoload dependencies; its live displays still bind to the shared real-traffic interface.

Added an output-equivalent fast path for the default pixel presentation and disabled redundant blending in the two fully opaque screen passes, retaining cinematic optics and the complete legacy treatment paths.

releases.title: Skydeck Launch Update
releases.summary: A complete aviation-first rebuild of Cloudline Launcher: direct build selection, real in-game moments, clear patch notes, and a flight-deck launch flow.
notes: Rebuilt the complete launcher visual system around launching a game, not browsing a library: sky-blue airspace visuals, flight-deck navigation, square instrument-panel geometry, direct build selection, concise patch notes, and a dedicated launch station. The established Cloudline logo remains intact.

Every release now has a dedicated hero image captured from that release's actual running Tower or Cockpit game window. The selected version changes both the live capture and its deterministic soft grain/scan treatment, so the image remains grounded in the build being launched rather than generic promotional art.
The selected build, its public or DSK-restricted state, offline availability, patch notes, history, and session-only developer access are now readable in one game-first launch flow.
AR-2.6.0 is the latest public launcher release. The staged AR-3.0.x builds remain above it in the catalogue and require Developer Secret Key clearance before launch.

releases.title: Developer Clearance Staging
releases.summary: Introduces the public release channel and an explicit Developer Secret Key gate for staged development builds.
notes: The Cloudline launch deck now includes a Developer Secret Key (DSK) field beside PLAY. Restricted builds identify themselves in the version picker and cannot launch until their key is verified for the current launcher session.
An invalid key receives a direct clearance-denied message. The launcher stores only a one-way verification hash; the DSK is neither displayed nor saved to launcher settings.

AR-3.0.0 is now a restricted development build. AR-2.5.0 remains the latest public offline release, and the complete public AR-1.7.8 through AR-2.5.0 library is still bundled, version-selectable, and playable offline.
This starts Cloudline's staged-release policy: new builds remain behind DSK clearance for developer testing until deliberately promoted into the public release library.

releases.title: Camera Stability & Frame Pacing
releases.summary: Eliminates the repeating chase-camera pulse and spreads live weather-map work across frames without reducing visual fidelity.
notes: Gate 5's apron-safe chase view is now a one-shot spawn assist with a release margin, so taxiing around the terminal boundary cannot switch the camera back and forth between two offsets.

Chase FOV now changes continuously with airspeed, and weather movement is a restrained irregular transverse vibration instead of a large synchronized bob. Gusts no longer feel like a recurring camera zoom.

Weather Radar and Wind Field preserve their complete previous image while their live replacement is rasterized in small frame slices. Selecting either mode remains immediate, but the regular refresh cannot cause a single-frame CPU spike.

Tiny wet-surface and weather-darkness changes are coalesced before mutating all airport materials or reapplying sky/light state. Cockpit, weather-navigation, radar smoke, clear/storm performance, launcher, archive, and packaged-snapshot checks passed before AR-2.4.2 entered the offline library.

releases.title: Regional Weather Performance
releases.summary: Keeps full moving-weather fidelity while removing the radar map stalls that could cripple performance in storms.
notes: Weather Radar now evaluates direct precipitation-cell reflectivity while drawing its texture, instead of repeatedly running terrain/coast, airport, and flight-condition calculations for every radar pixel.

Wind Field uses smooth four-point interpolation over its real sampled grid rather than blending every wind sample against every output pixel. The visual remains continuous and the underlying local wind simulation is unchanged.
Terminal wind updates and radar sweeps no longer force a full field-texture rebuild each frame. Weather and Wind modes retain their live updates at a stable cadence without the severe stutter.
Storm, fog, Weather Radar, Wind Field, game, launcher, archive, and packaged-snapshot regression checks passed before AR-2.4.1 entered the offline library.

releases.title: Dynamic Regional Weather
releases.summary: Adds travelling storm cells, local flying weather, live radar and imperfect forecasts across the complete archipelago.
notes: Moving weather cells now travel between Mason County and every destination island. Rain, fog, cloud ceiling, visibility, gusts, lightning risk, terrain turbulence, coastal crosswinds, and wind shear are sampled at the aircraft or field rather than applied world-wide.

Weather radar renders the real cell returns and reports local ceiling and shear. The Tower Weather desk supplies a +30-minute forecast with confidence and deliberate uncertainty, so a convective forecast can be wrong.

Wet runways gain visible standing water and reduced braking. Local wind changes runway selection; severe visibility, wind shear, or flooding automatically closes a strip and returns it to service only after conditions improve.

Dirt strips retain heavy-rain moisture, become muddy, close when unusable, prevent player takeoff, and cause regional commuter flights to wait or reroute. Regional-weather, game, launcher, archive, and packaged-snapshot regression checks passed before AR-2.4.0 entered the offline library.

releases.title: Full CRT Curvature & Scrolling Library
releases.summary: Restores the full convex TV picture bend with accurate curved-screen clicks and makes the launcher catalog scrollable.
notes: TV Mode now applies its original barrel-bent convex picture across the full treated display, including Affect HUD & interface. Pointer events map through the exact shader transform, so a visually curved control receives its click at the location the player sees.
The Settings dialog remains above the post-process layer and uses ordinary coordinates. The treatment cursor reasserts native-pointer hiding via both input and display-server APIs every active frame.
The launcher version selector is limited to a compact 320-pixel popup and automatically provides a scrollbar for the complete offline release history instead of listing every version at once.
Curved-input, settings, cursor, game, launcher, archive, and packaged-snapshot regression checks passed before AR-2.3.2 entered the offline launcher library.

releases.title: CRT Curvature & Cursor Correction
releases.summary: Restores the original convex TV picture bend while preserving accurate controls and a single treatment-aware cursor.
notes: TV Mode once again barrel-bends and stretches the world picture toward its rounded CRT bezel, with the original convex curved-face character restored.

The bend is deliberately confined to the world pass. Affect HUD & interface retains CRT glass, vignette, and signal treatment without moving interactive controls away from their real input coordinates; Settings remains crisp above every treatment pass.
Affect mouse cursor now actively re-hides the OS cursor after focus changes and on every frame while its rendered pointer is active, preventing the native pointer from appearing on top.
Curvature, coordinate safety, settings, and cursor handoff regression coverage passed before this immutable AR-2.3.1 source snapshot was added to the offline launcher library.

releases.title: Flight Fidelity & Television Repair
releases.summary: Repairs coordinate-safe CRT presentation and rebuilds the Cockpit engine, flap, and take-off simulation around live aircraft conditions.
notes: TV Mode no longer displaces the visible cursor from actual input coordinates. Settings stays crisp above the treatment pass, ON/OFF labels remain visible, and opening it with O keeps the live scene running behind the overlay.

The analogue signal now uses bowed and broken scan segments, irregular sync streaks, travelling hold noise, snow, and small row-level wander. Every World treatment resets its shader state live, including while TV Mode remains enabled.

Fuel flow now responds continuously to delayed power, density altitude, speed and propeller load, climb/descent work, and manoeuvring. OIL and EGT gain independent thermal lag, cooling, run-time, and sustained-power stress behavior.

Flaps deploy physically over time, receive a dedicated live HUD readout, materially increase lift and drag, change stall speed by actual position, and identify their live position in an overspeed warning.

Take-off now builds through speed-dependent rotation, flap-dependent wing lift, and sustained back pressure: the nose rises first and crossing 62 knots alone can no longer lift the aircraft. Full game and launcher regression suites pass for this immutable offline snapshot.

releases.title: Expanded Islands & Vintage Television
releases.summary: Transforms the destination islands into a larger, wilder archipelago and adds an authentic analogue-TV visual mode with optional cursor and curved-glass treatment.
notes: All twelve destination islands are now full-scale landmasses with much broader, irregular low-poly coasts, clear channels, expanded landing fields, accessible airspace, and strategic camera coverage.

Settlements no longer follow repeated tidy layouts. Larger villages, uneven lanes, varied terrain parcels, scattered gardens and rocks, denser forests, and randomized low-poly wilderness clusters make every island feel inhabited and distinct.
VINTAGE TV is a new visual treatment with softened analogue signal, scanlines, luminance flutter, and intermittent horizontal bright/dark sync interference rather than constant digital static.

Visual settings now include Affect mouse cursor, which swaps in a treatment-aware in-game cursor, and TV Mode, an independent convex CRT-glass display shape with rounded bezel corners and edge vignette that layers over every world treatment.

The menu overview, exploration bounds, review viewpoints, cockpit archipelago airspace, and ocean coverage expand with the region. Full game, launcher, settings, cockpit, safety, smoke, and render-profile tests passed before this immutable release snapshot was added to the offline library.

releases.title: Operational Archipelago
releases.summary: Makes all twelve destination islands fully operational with corrected roofs and roads, local weather, regional traffic, flyable runways, and dirt-specific touchdown effects.
notes: Every island cabin roof now rises to a proper ridge. The road system is rebuilt as continuous village loops and purposeful spurs, with hamlets and ferries kept on the settlement side of each runway and automated checks preventing road/runway crossings.

Six autonomous commuter aircraft now rotate among all twelve island fields through gate, taxi, takeoff, climb, cruise, approach, landing, and taxi-in phases without entering Mason County's controller queue.

Cloud coverage and the spatial wind field span the full archipelago. Every island windsock is live, the radar follows selected regional aircraft, and crosswind is calculated against the local destination runway.

Cockpit mode recognizes every paved and dirt island strip as a real runway for aligned landings and complete takeoffs, with expanded terrain and airspace coverage plus dirt-specific rolling resistance.

Dirt strips no longer carry pavement-style dashed lines. Their touchdowns generate persistent ochre gear-contact dust, while paved fields preserve tyre smoke and rain spray. Close and strategic visual audits cover multiple islands, local wind, regional flight, roads, roofs, runways, and effects.

releases.title: Living Archipelago Expansion
releases.summary: Rebuilds the western sea as twelve large, widely separated destination islands with complete airfields, settlements, working districts, and distinct coasts.
notes: Twelve materially larger islands now occupy a broad western archipelago with clear blue-water channels between neighbors and substantial separation from Mason County; every island remains smaller than the main island.

Every destination has an inland paved or dirt runway with a five-unit grass safety area, compact apron, two or three marked stands, terminal, beacon tower, windsock, parked commuter aircraft, and connected access roads.

Primary villages, secondary hamlets, ferry landings, utilities, remote homesteads, groves, terrain parcels, trails, gardens, and working districts fill the expanded acreage while preserving each island's lighthouse, port, sanctuary, lookout, tidepool, farm, forest, weather, quarry, or northern identity.

Fourteen-point coves and headlands, varied grass setbacks, biome-specific sand and shingle, accent strands, shallow shelves, and sea stacks replace the repeated beach rings. Detached foam bars are removed and ocean depth shading follows the new archipelago footprint.

Expanded ocean coverage, camera travel, strategic framing, and vessel routes support the new region. Geometry regression checks and repeated strategic plus close visual reviews cover island scale, spacing, landscape density, landing facilities, and runway clear zones.

releases.title: Retro Low-Poly Ocean
releases.summary: Reconstructs Cloudline's flat cyan water as a faceted, depth-layered sea and grounds every craft with proper waterlines and wakes.
notes: The former four-vertex transparent sheet is now a 9,600-triangle displaced ocean with stepped retro swell, calculated normals, angular colour facets, and restrained crest highlights.
Broken shallow, shelf, and deep-water regions replace the uniformly bright cyan floor with a readable teal-to-navy sense of depth around both the main island and archipelago.
Every moving craft is calibrated to its keel and gains a polygonal waterline contact plus paired stern foam; moored scenery boats receive matching surface contact.
Detached projected boat shadows are removed. Flat directional diamond wakes stay on the sea instead of rising like smoke.
Ocean geometry, waterline height, shadow removal, and wake shape/height are regression-tested and the complete system was checked in a deterministic live water view.

releases.title: Verified Low-Poly Airfield
releases.summary: Reconstructs every airport surface, route, sign, light, and PAPI installation as one visually verified low-poly field.
notes: Runways, taxiways, apron, access roads, and parking are now flush polygon surfaces with no exposed slab sides or stacked plate intersections.
Taxiways A/B, runway entries, gate lead-ins, and angular perimeter routes use continuous mitered paint derived from shared route geometry; hold-short markings fit their entries exactly.
Compact route-facing signs sit outside all movement surfaces. Square runway and taxi lights are recalculated from exact centerline, edge, threshold, and connector constants.
Runway paint is completely flat and shadowless. PAPI uses compact supported housings outside the runway edge and continues to guide both AI and player approaches.
Geometry assertions, full gameplay tests, and six captured live viewpoints independently verified the rebuilt airfield.

releases.title: Airfield Surface Rebuild
releases.summary: Rebuilds KMCA's tarmac, markings, PAPI, signs, and ground lights as one coherent retro airfield.
notes: Runways, taxiways, and apron now use a deliberate surface hierarchy with a single clean paint elevation, removing the overlapping, flickering tarmac treatment.
Taxi routes now use restrained centrelines, edge lights, aligned hold-short bars, short gate lead-ins, and traffic-facing signs instead of directional-arrow clutter.
PAPI bars are physically supported and approach-facing; they now show the player aircraft a live visual glide indication during a lined-up approach.
Circular movement-area lights are now hard-edged rectangular fixtures with unchanged illumination. Automated grounding checks verify their bases meet the pavement or terrain beneath them.

releases.title: Gate 5 Camera Clearance
releases.summary: Makes Camera 1 frame the aircraft instead of terminal geometry at the Cockpit spawn.
notes: Camera 1's original rear chase position was inside the terminal/hangar roof volume at Gate 5, which hid the player aircraft.
It now starts from an open-apron shoulder position and automatically returns to its normal wide chase frame after the aircraft taxis clear.
Added a spawn framing regression check.

releases.title: Flight View & Controls Correction
releases.summary: Keeps the undercarriage view above pavement and corrects flap and rudder presentation.
notes: Undercarriage Camera stays low in flight but now clears local terrain during taxi, touchdown, and rollout so tyre smoke remains visible.
Flaps now deploy downward. A/D animate only ailerons and steer on the ground; Z visibly commands left rudder and X right rudder.
Added control-surface and ground-camera regression coverage.

releases.title: Fixed External Cameras
releases.summary: Adds rigid close-chase and low undercarriage views to Cockpit flight.
notes: Locked Chase Camera is hard-mounted to the airframe, immediately inheriting pitch, yaw, and bank instead of using chase smoothing.
Undercarriage Camera is mounted behind and below the main gear, looking forward across the wheels, fuselage underside, and aircraft nose.
C now cycles five flight perspectives: chase, wing, close follow, locked chase, and undercarriage.

releases.title: Flight HUD Treatment Fix
releases.summary: Makes Affect HUD & interface apply to the Cockpit HUD as its setting states.
notes: Removed the Cockpit-only rendering override introduced with the terminal HUD refit.
With Affect HUD & interface disabled, retro grain, dither, and CRT treatment stay behind the flight HUD on the rendered world.
With it enabled, the same treatment now includes every Cockpit HUD element, including analog flight instruments and the power panel.

releases.title: Station Card Focus Repair

notes: The full-card transparent Button was drawing the new opaque terminal focus style above the Cockpit card’s image and copy.
Station hit targets now remain transparent in every state; the existing card overlay supplies the visible hover and keyboard-focus treatment instead.
Both station backdrops and copy layers are now named and explicitly ordered, with a regression test that verifies each remains loaded and visible.

releases.title: Terminal HUD Refit
releases.summary: Rebuilds the Tower and Cockpit screen language as a hard-edged Cloudline aviation terminal while preserving the analog pilot instruments.
notes: Replaced rounded cards, soft shadows, and repeated nested outlines with opaque terminal panels, single borders, square controls, monospaced operational text, and Cloudline cream, sky, mint, amber, coral, and red status colours.
Tower adds a shared KMCA terminal frame, a flatter command terminal and radar treatment, and decision cards that show urgency with one coloured left rail.
Cockpit preserves the analog flight deck and power quadrant. The flight world behind them now always receives the selected retro screen treatment, while the physical instruments remain clear.
Added terminal HUD regression coverage and a saved AR-1.7.13 source snapshot.

releases.title: Built-In Release Library

notes: Running game/project.godot from Godot now opens Cloudline Launcher first. The transient game process stays minimized and exits before a game screen is drawn.
Every currently archived release is built into the launcher as an offline snapshot. PLAY is enabled for each available version without a manifest server or download.
Built-in archives and retained extracted releases now share a 1 GiB verified storage budget. Selecting an older built-in release no longer evicts another extracted built-in version.
Clear Cache removes only local extracted builds and downloaded packages. Saves, career data, preferences, the catalog, and the release archives embedded in the launcher remain intact.

releases.title: Working Flight Library

notes: Home, all-version history, version-specific release notes, and launcher settings are separate working screens.
Credits now live inside Launcher Settings; the former standalone Credits tab has been removed.
The selected 1.7.8 build is archived as an immutable source snapshot and starts from the launcher in a local Godot run.
Flight controls no longer taper or self-level while held: excessive pitch, bank, yaw, or low speed now reaches the existing physical stall and departure behavior.
Cleared the runway centreline block from the 27L/27R threshold-designator zone and matched the game cursor to the launcher’s native system cursor.

releases.title: Launchable Source Snapshot
releases.summary: Repairs the saved-release handoff so PLAY opens the selected snapshot instead of a blank blue window.
notes: Source snapshots now include Godot's required imported-texture and global-class cache alongside the game project.
Verified a freshly extracted snapshot can start its menu through the launcher handoff without missing-resource errors.
Rebuilt the AR-1.7.8 archive with the same required runtime cache so it is playable too.

releases.title: Snapshot Recovery Check

notes: The launcher now validates the imported-resource and global-class cache before treating a saved snapshot as installed.

releases.title: Launcher-First Desktop Patch
releases.summary: Makes Cloudline Launcher the primary desktop entry point with a corrected Dock icon and shared Cloudline cursor.
notes: Rebuilt the launcher application mark with a smaller optical footprint, transparent safe area, and a rounded inset frame that follows the tile corners.
Configured the launcher as the macOS app entry point, including its native Dock/Finder icon and a versioned macOS export preset.

Clear Cache now explains that it removes only downloaded packages and extracted builds; saves, career data, the catalog, bundled snapshots, and launcher preferences stay intact.

release_history.title: Flight Fidelity & Television Repair

release_history.title: Dynamic Regional Weather

release_history.title: The Living Archipelago
notes: November 12 physical hub: 98 native workflow/systems checks, 29 safety checks, 20 desktop checks and 15 continuous-path checks pass. 7 focused full-resolution native views average 59.95–60.34 FPS with shaders and active simulation.
Enter Mason County replaces the main Enter button; Pilot Logbook moves into the computer while all existing progression and records are retained. The temporary Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P shortcut is removed.

One continuous camera path flies from the actual menu view into Hangar 01, up the actual stairs and to a randomly selected physical computer; longer fades transfer to the seated NPC. Desktop logout follows the saved path in reverse and fades the orange menu back in.

Five physical workstations have CRT housings, 97 separately shaped and labelled keyboard keys, a wired moving mouse and a fitted right hand. The monitor cursor stays inside the computer; the rebindable look key permits looking away for power controls.

Hold the rebindable computer-power key K for three seconds. The computer starts off; select or confirm an app before powering off and standing up. Every new walking, seat, power and look action is rebindable.
Cloudline Desk 95 adds distinct desktop app logos with names underneath, icon-only taskbar buttons, the Cloudline Start logo, live date/time, searchable app results with Open actions and logout.

Flight Deck offers one real career contract with the actual remaining Shuffle allowance. Cloudline Writer has an editable document, font family/size, bold, italic, underline, clipboard, undo/redo, insert/date/bullets, reading/editing views and session draft saving. Scroll to the signature and sign to activate the actual transport mission.

Air Traffic Control offers 10/15/30-minute duty periods, a live world journey map and four world markers following the open apron around the terminal. Walk into the tower and use Y on a console chair to fade into the existing ATC view; leave the chair to return to walking.

Minigames library, online/offline choices and matchmaking stay inside the physical monitor. Starting a match uses the existing game; Return to Menu automatically seats the character at the same live workstation. Pilot Logbook uses the preserved career/fleet/service record renderer.
Mode assignments change at Hangar 01 computers. Desktop logout returns to the orange main menu; an early ATC departure returns to the physical player rather than teleporting to a mode picker.

Aircraft contacts now confirm registry ownership, current visible source mesh and pose. Self/effect/stale contacts are ignored, occupied cabin surfaces remain pinned, and repositioning clears contact sweeps. A slow taxi bump stops the aircraft rather than causing immediate flight over.
All cabin seats accept a half-second Y hold. Copilot and passenger chairs have no flight authority; only the captain can start or fly. The copilot yoke is lowered and shortened to clear the panel.

Propellers combine actual spinning blades with a filtered dark blade exposure and blur disc in first person. Aborted starting and engine shutdown coast down according to actual shaft RPM, including a longer stop from full power.

Cockpit controls use smaller target radii. Aim at the physical throttle for E/Q; both separated callouts appear together. Hands are fitted nearer the yoke, and aircraft camera motion adds a subtle speed-dependent vibration.

Inverted controls defaults on: the bound pitch-up action points the nose down, and the bound pitch-down action raises it. Turning inversion off restores their usual direction; rebinding still works across civil and fighter flight.

Battery consumption uses real elapsed time so reading dispatch cannot flatten the parked aircraft on the accelerated career clock. Actual out-of-limit instruments pulse with red dial outlines and audible alerts in every camera. Persistent oil/temperature/RPM abuse reduces engine power; prolonged overspeed damages structure. Startup grace and debounce avoid false pressure alarms during normal cranking.
Indoor performance uses exact opaque-wall occluders and bounded monitor-map updates while retaining native image resolution, geometry, materials and shadows.

Two requested rollback checkpoints are retained outside the project: before all changes and after aircraft repairs before the hub. Current source ZIP/cache and all-release comparison are refreshed; all authentic Alpha archives remain unchanged. No compiled app or EXE is packaged. Public launch/countdown remain November 21, 2026, 4:30 PM CST.

Hold C for smooth 2.6x optical zoom toward the current gaze; release C smoothly restores normal view. V cycles flight cameras; the previous default C-camera binding migrates to V.

Oil quantity is an eight-quart-capacity consumed store. Pump pressure responds to RPM, temperature and supply; starvation affects lubrication health/power. CHT and EGT follow load/cooling rather than decorative RPM labels.

Electrical gauges show stored battery charge/current and alternator bus voltage, including master-off and engine-off discharge. Engine-driven vacuum spins up/down the attitude and heading gyros; low-pressure/fuel/voltage/vacuum lamps use those states.

Physical readings update at 29.42 Hz in the focused native run; static engraved artwork is cached at double panel resolution. The external engine HUD shares the same pressure, quantity, temperature, voltage, current and vacuum state.

§ THE LIVING ARCHIPELAGO — THE WORLD

Every destination is an authored place rather than generic island scenery: Juniper Reach, Skylark, Gullhaven, Granite Point, Northwatch, Beacon Harbor, Port Halcyon, Meadowmere, Sanctuary Bay, Lookout Cove, Tidepool Landing and Harbor Point each have a named town, an economic district, a marina, an emergency facility, an airfield and an offshore port anchor.

Each island carries its own role and identity — farming, forestry, quarrying, weather station, lighthouse, fishing cove, wildflower meadows, bird sanctuary, lookout, tidepools and harbor — which shapes its buildings, land use and the cargo it needs.

Road-locked scheduled ground traffic brings the towns to life: cars, cargo trucks, buses, emergency vehicles, residents and terminal travelers follow explicit town-to-terminal-to-worksite-to-marina anchor chains and yield in lane instead of being shoved off the road.

Scheduled marine traffic runs on validated routes — ferries, fishing boats and a cargo barge with proper hull variants, wakes, operating hours and port metadata — and no water route is ever created unless every segment clears the island coastlines.
Daily construction closures visibly drop barriers and hold cargo traffic, and dent local satisfaction while they are active.

Weather or an explicit isolation state can suspend an island's air service, hold its commuter legs, grow its unmet demand, and update the tower's live island-accessibility board so you can see which fields are open.
The strategic island-overview camera was reframed and the animated ocean and seabed were expanded well past the view bounds so the map can never expose an ocean edge.
§ THE TRANSPORT CAREER — THE JOB
Cockpit mode is now a full airline job rather than a sandbox: you are dispatched real work, flown start to finish under tower control.

The tower talks you through the entire flight — clearance, taxi, hold short, cleared for takeoff, departure, enroute, approach, cleared to land, taxi to stand, and offload — with each instruction shown in a readable band and logged to a comms history.
A glowing, mitered route ribbon lights the exact taxi and routing path directly on the pavement, so you always know where to go on the ground.
Numbered 1-to-N waypoints drop in the world and on the map in order and tick off as you reach them, replacing guesswork with a clear route to fly.

Missions are procedurally generated and weather-aware: the active runway follows the wind, dirt strips close in rain, and payload weight feeds the takeoff model, so the combinations are effectively endless.
Multi-island chains string several legs together with a chain bonus, and a standing-contracts layer (Supply Run, Lifelines, Grand Tour and more) tracks long-term goals across many flights.
§ SIGNABLE PAPER CONTRACTS

Every accepted job is a readable paper charter you must actually read and sign before it begins — headed CONTRACT #N (your lifetime completed count), it names a real client drawn from the destination town's economy (its marina, district, facility or council) with that counterparty's signature already on the page.

The charter lists the consignment, the full leg-by-leg routing, the delivery window, the consideration (Advancement Points plus Flight Credits), and four to five generated terms and conditions, so combined with the procedural routing the contract text is effectively never repeated.
At the bottom is a SIGN HERE box: click it, type your aircraft's tail number, and SIGN & ACCEPT to start the job — or request a different charter instead.

Ultra-rare charters (about 5%) are issued by the Office of the Territorial Governor on sealed-blue official stock rather than the usual parchment, carry a confidential 'sealed' clause and a much larger payout, and unlock a hidden achievement.
Signing your first contract unlocks the 'Ink on Paper' achievement.
§ THE MISSION BOARD

§ ATC & NAVIGATION — RULES THAT ENFORCE

The flight lifecycle is strict and actually checked: route waypoints are consumed in order (reaching a later one early does nothing), you must stop and HOLD SHORT and wait before a takeoff clearance is issued, and entering the runway before you are cleared is a logged incursion.
Departing without a clearance, departing on the wrong runway or heading (more than 55 degrees off), or landing at a field you were not cleared for are all detected violations.
Departure detection is latched so it fires exactly once per leg on first lift-off, instead of relying on a single frame that could be missed — so these violations are caught reliably.
Every violation records an ATC reprimand, applies an Advancement-Point and reputation penalty, and shows an unmistakable red on-screen notice.
The tower now reads a real computed heading on departure ('fly heading 073 direct BKN') and the correct runway heading on approach.

Enroute fixes are generated densely along each leg (roughly every 420 m) as lit floor beacons — a spreading pulse pad with a vertical beam — so the path to fly is always visible, and island arrivals get a clear lit taxi path from the runway to the stand.
The Journey Map draws three lines at once: blue to the island, green to your next mission waypoint, and magenta to your own placed waypoint.
§ THE ECONOMY — DELIVERIES THAT MATTER
Every island carries a real, lazily-accruing transport demand, seeded per island and growing over time — faster for weathered, unpaved strips that rely more on air service.
Completing a delivery writes the units back and drops that island's backlog, so your flying actually changes the regional picture.
The mission generator weights destinations by demand and applies surge pricing, so a starved, high-demand field can pay up to 1.8 times the base.
The aircraft inspector surfaces each flight's regional cargo and passenger outcome so you can see the effect of a delivery.
§ FLIGHT MODEL — EARN THE LIFT
Automatic takeoff is gone: lift-off is solely a pilot action — hold the rotation input at or above the 62-knot rotation speed on a usable runway.
A sustained-climb contract keeps your commanded power and pitch through the first rotation transition, giving the wing time to build lift instead of dropping straight back onto the runway.

Takeoff is a multi-factor model: flap setting, head/tailwind (a headwind shortens the roll, a tailwind lengthens it), crosswind (the airframe weathercocks and drifts and must be held with rudder), engine RPM and spool state, and an over-rotation penalty that drags the tail if you haul the nose up too early.

The rudder is a genuine aerodynamic control: the pedals command sideslip, the nose swings off the flight path, a side force gradually curves the track, dihedral rolls the aircraft, sideslip costs drag, and holding uncoordinated rudder near the stall departs the wing.
The departure runway is chosen for where you are going, balancing headwind against pointing toward your destination (a strong wind still wins for safety).

The analog propeller gauge was rebuilt so its pointer, tick labels, operating arcs and digital readout share one literal 0-5,000 RPM scale with a smooth fixed-pitch response, replacing the old linear ramp and yellow-range wall.

A runway-only rotation-assist exists purely as an input-safety net if a platform drops the held pitch-up event with takeoff power established; manual rotation always commits immediately at Vr, and grass, apron, taxiway and unusable dirt are never auto-rotated.

§ CRASH, IMPACT & DITCHING PHYSICS

Severity-based impact handling covers terrain, runways, buildings, aircraft, ground vehicles, vessels and water: relative velocity, impact attitude, object scale and surface type determine debris, flash and fire, smoke, spray, reciprocal aircraft damage, and controlled-versus-destructive ditching.

Every effect uses bounded low-poly geometry for stable performance — a single emissive pixel burst, one faceted flash, and at most a few low-poly smoke puffs — with no cone flames or stray flying-debris nodes.

Aircraft-to-aircraft impacts use a reciprocal two-body momentum response; runway collisions send both aircraft into speed-sensitive skids with wet-surface braking, and airborne collisions preserve the remaining motion, rotation and gravity-driven fall instead of freezing either airframe.

A player-ending impact transitions directly into an input-locked, monochrome live aftermath: the crash physics, explosion, smoke, skid or fall keep progressing in real time with no reset, pause, settings, camera or exit controls, then present Flight Over with Gate 5 respawn and airport-menu choices.
Crash-grounding is rebuilt around the measured aircraft bounds so wings, nose, tail, wheels and model corners stay above the actual terrain while a damaged aircraft skids or settles.

In the transport job, a crash fails the active contract permanently (you can never draw that same contract again), applies a severe penalty scaled by impact severity, and draws a fresh charter on respawn.

Every drop in this cycle was verified on Godot 4.7.2 with a clean full-project parse and compile, plus dedicated headless harnesses exercising the contract generator and sign flow, the penalty/reputation/achievement APIs, demand accrual and write-back, surge pricing, the mission board, island taxi routing, the 50-achievement roster, the fleet unlocks and the Free-Flight rank gate.

Full-loop regression tests drive takeoff climb-out and short-final landings through the exact per-frame flight and obstacle pass the live game runs, including a no-auto-takeoff assertion that a full-power roll past Vr stays on the ground until the pilot rotates.

Exact collision sampling is capped at a safe rate, caches active ground vehicles, and broad-rejects distant aircraft and vehicles before detailed probes, to keep a high frame rate without removing collision coverage.
§ DEVELOPER-BUILD NOTES
BR-1.0.0 is public and playable directly from the launcher. It remains a separate bundled snapshot, so edits to the working tree cannot silently change an earlier catalog version.

On Mac and Windows, launcher PLAY installs the fingerprinted BR source snapshot and its matching compiled native game, then starts that compiled game. The source archive remains complete for verification and fallback. A rebuilt same-version package changes its SHA-256, so the launcher replaces stale installed bytes on the next PLAY without a version bump.
Mouse flight aim now spans the game window and gains tiny movement-only response variations for a more tactile aircraft feel.

Convoy Strike joins the minigames as the second card. Fifteen attackers face fifteen defenders over four random islands carrying 50–100 vehicles each. Attackers must destroy every envoy before the 15-minute clock; defenders win if any survive.

The convoy fleet uses SIpriv CC BY 4.0 BTR 82, Gepard, Humvee, BM 30 Smerch, S300, and parked SU-37 models. Radar and launcher variants use their authored animations or deployment poses. Gepards and S300s launch unlimited missiles with a 25–30-second cooldown.

All three fighters carry bombs with different strike strengths. Press V in keyboard flight or right click in mouse flight; a bomb returns every 15 seconds, and a final envoy kill immediately grants one. The HUD shows a predicted impact marker, island health bar, fleet count, 15-minute timer, team colors, and friendly lock protection. Aircraft and defenders respawn during the match.
Mouse flight now responds more strongly as the aim ring approaches a window corner, with precise control near the centre.

The Convoy Strike mission window now shows live target count, island health, team strength, bomb pips, and recharge progress. The mission timer uses an outlined face without the old rectangular backing.

Convoy Strike now keeps aircraft inside the finite rendered world. A warning area starts well before the ocean edge, and a hard boundary resolves through the normal death and respawn flow. Battle Royale boundary rendering also skips close-up stripe shading to avoid a full-screen slowdown.

The Convoy Strike mission board now matches the gray Windows 95 armament panel while retaining its island, team, and bomb readouts. Ground-to-air missile cooldown varies from 30 seconds with a full defense network toward 25 seconds as launchers are destroyed; opening shots are staggered.

Convoy Strike now has 15 attackers and 15 defenders. Respawns reuse each fighter's imported model instead of rebuilding it during combat. The shared kill feed now detaches rows before deferred deletion, fixing an infinite loop that could freeze or crash after several kills. Distance fog hides the finite map edge at high altitude in both minigames.

Mouse flight now uses continuous relative input, with hidden capture restored immediately after respawn. Ground launchers still have 25–30-second individual cooldowns, but their network spaces launches at least five seconds apart, limits simultaneous missiles, and sends only one at a time toward each jet. Their shorter engagement range gives attackers room to approach.
The aircraft picker remains hidden through the final loading frames and appears only after the loading cover has fully faded away in Battle Royale and Convoy Strike.

The Living Archipelago now uses 24 individual Creative Mango road vehicles, including a rare F1 car, with animated tire meshes. Traffic follows island grades and Mason County's real sloped tunnel portals; camper trailers are omitted. Island road links, the terminal's east return road, and Sanctuary Island's stilted lookout boardwalk are expanded. Creative Mango's CC BY 4.0 attribution appears in the launcher credits.

Convoy Strike now lets the player defend. Choose one of the three fighters with bombing disabled and right-click missile fire, or select an S-300 ground launcher at a random island airfield. Its vehicle camera, air-search scope, timed lock, eight missiles, 15-second launch cooldown, 30-second missile resupply, and bonus missile every two kills make ground defense playable. Holding R for three seconds sacrifices the current unit and reopens the role picker without restarting the match.

Ground S-300 defense has three C-key views: optic, launcher, and tactical. The selected launcher rack follows mouse aim, and every aircraft kill displays +1 KILL even alongside a missile reward. Island houses have rebuilt continuous roofs, gable walls, windows, doors, and varied porch details; the roof panels no longer cut through the walls. Batched house trim keeps island rendering lighter.

November 10 cinematic atmosphere rebuild: sunrise and sunset now follow solar elevation, with a gold horizon, rose/lavender twilight, cooler upper sky and a gradual blue-hour transition. A bounded HDR sun core and layered aureole retain bright sun shots without whitening the whole archipelago.

Unified cinematic world and Photo Mode lighting: warm low-angle sunlight, cooler ambient fill, directional cloud shading and copper/silver cloud rims follow the same solar palette. Photo time/weather controls retain their overrides and restore the original environment on exit.

Reworked the cinematic lens finish with multi-scale highlight diffusion, luminance-masked warm highlights/cool shadows, restrained sun diffraction, an anamorphic streak and additive lens ghosts. Sky precision noise removes packed-HDR night banding without restoring a retro dither treatment.

Fixed cinematic post-processing being erased by the later pixel/CRT pass. An explicit back-buffer copy now composes both passes, preserving the native HUD unless its treatment setting is enabled. The shader switch disables cinematic optics and restores baseline sunlight.

Water now has a tighter enhanced specular response and stronger true Photo Mode reflections, carrying the new sunrise/sunset palette over the swell. Full-resolution Photo Mode retains its separate reflection render; normal gameplay retains the existing single-world rendering approach.

Cinematic rendering verification: five time-of-day captures plus storm and lunar views; shader, weather-fog, moon, UI/cursor and Photo Mode restoration checks passed. Six focused Apple M4 source views averaged 85.37–153.17 FPS at 1280×800, shaders enabled, default 80% and saved 51% pixelation. These bounded averages are not Windows, long-session or guaranteed minimum-frame results.

Decoupled the reusable ATC tower from game/menu scene classes so standalone model tools and headless fixtures load without pulling in gameplay autoload dependencies; its live displays still bind to the shared real-traffic interface.

Added an output-equivalent fast path for the default pixel presentation and disabled redundant blending in the two fully opaque screen passes, retaining cinematic optics and the complete legacy treatment paths.
